_status: DRY-RUN — read-only. No curation write performed.
_ruling: Sam's PER-LADDER level sets, authored 2026-08-24 and stored as data at kb/reference/esl_level_sets.json. Supersedes his own absolute bands 0-2/3-5/6-10 from earlier the same day, which superseded the P-4 pinning.

_noncredit_shift._about: A NONCREDIT course sits one band BELOW where its college's ladder rung would put a credit course, because noncredit ESL is generally preparation FOR college ESL. Applied ONLY on the ladder path — a course stating its level in words keeps it.
_noncredit_shift._why: Sam, first on NOCE — "1=B and 2=I (because it is NC, it is generally a prep course for college ESL)" — then "Scope it to NC not just NOCE" when it was implemented as a single-institution override.
_noncredit_shift._source: credit_status, per COURSE, from kb/coci_minted_memberships.json UNION kb/coci_minted_singletons.json['courses'], joined on control_number. 118,195 control numbers carry it; coverage over the ESL corpus is 100%.
_noncredit_shift._a_correction_worth_keeping: ⚠️ An earlier cut of this rule keyed on the spot-check worklist's `credit_type`, which is blank on 24% of members INCLUDING the NOCE courses Sam named — so it failed on his own example, and was propped up with a hand-listed set of wholly-noncredit institutions. Sam: "You should have data for each course as credit or noncredit." He was right; the authoritative per-course field existed in the COCI staging files all along. The institution list is GONE — do not reintroduce it. If this rule ever looks under-covered again, check the join before adding a hand-maintained list.

_resolution: A level WORD on the identity title wins; otherwise each member votes its own college's ladder reading and the identity takes the MODE. A tie is reported, never resolved by picking the safer band.

ladder_derivation.source: the whole published ESL corpus (unified_courses_data.js + unified_courses_members.js), NOT the folded worklist
ladder_derivation.rule: max rung observed over the whole ESL corpus, >= 2 distinct rungs, length 2-9; a 2-rung read abstains because Sam's table has no L=2 row

evidence_strength._read_this_first: A ladder vote can rest on a SINGLE member course, and the weakest tier of the level reader is a bare trailing integer ('Academic Writing 3'), which may be a sequence number rather than a rung. Both are reported per group because they decide whether a proposal is actionable, not merely correct.
